About

Canadian-born designer, based in Katowice, Poland for over a decade. I started in 2004 in desktop publishing, advertising and graphic design, working freelance with clients across North America, Europe and Asia, before moving in-house into design, marketing and, eventually, product UI/UX.

Today I’m a UI/UX designer at KLDiscovery, working on Nebula, an AI-powered enterprise eDiscovery platform, where I’ve helped shape the design system and visual direction from early product and engineering discussions through to launch.

I work best as a senior design voice, building future-facing solutions together, whether collaborating with product and engineering teams or working directly with clients. I’m hands-on, detail-oriented, and happiest when we’re sketching, talking and building side by side.

Process

Systems thinking, human feeling, thoughtful craft.

Good design doesn't need to shout. It brings people and ideas together and makes interactions feel natural. Thoughtful in structure, intentional in every detail. Design communicates ideas with clarity and purpose.

06

KB Structures · 2026 · Brand designer

KB Structures

A complete identity for a structural engineering consultancy: logo, visual system, guidelines and a branded Word document suite the team uses every day.

Role
Brand identity, guidelines and document system
Deliverables
Logo, visual system, brand guidelines, Word templates for proposals, reports and correspondence

The brief

A structural engineering consultancy needed an identity that signalled precision and technical credibility.

The mark

The logo interlocks a K and a B into a single monogram, drawn on a construction grid of circles and angled guides. A heavy, even outline gives it the precision of a technical drawing, and a warm orange fills the counters. It sits beside a simple wordmark: KB in bold, STRUCTURES widely spaced.

The identity

A restrained visual system built around that mark: a yellow accent, grey and yellow dot patterns, and photo-collage illustrations that set black-and-white buildings against yellow shapes, bar charts and risk symbols. The monogram's outline also works as a large background graphic.

Built for daily use

A brand only works if people use it. The document system covers proposals, reports and client correspondence as Word templates, so engineers produce on-brand documents without needing a designer.

Outcome

Delivered a complete brand package: logo, guidelines and a suite of branded Word documents.

Kroll · Duff & Phelps · 2016 – 2019 · Senior Marketing Associate: art direction and design

Global Fraud & Risk Report

Art direction and design for Kroll's annual flagship report, built from a blank page in 2016 and evolved across four editions and more than ten regional versions.

Role
Art direction and design: visual system, covers, layouts and data visualisation
Scope
Four annual editions, 10+ regional editions, print and digital
Readers
C-suite and risk professionals worldwide

The brief

An annual flagship publication covering global fraud, cyber and risk trends, and one of the firm's most visible pieces of thought leadership. It needed to read as authoritative and current every year, in every regional edition.

Art direction

I developed the report's visual system from scratch in 2016, then evolved it across four annual editions: keeping it recognisably the same report while refreshing the visual language each year. Each cover set the mood for that edition's theme, from the faceted globe of 2016 to the storm-front photography of 2019/20.

Data visualisation

The heart of the report is survey data. The Global Risk Map spread and the regional pages turn hundreds of data points into a visual language readers can scan quickly and compare across regions.

Production at scale

Coordinated with regional offices and external printers across multiple languages and formats, keeping every edition consistent with the master design.

Outcome

Distributed to thousands of C-suite and risk professionals worldwide. Editions include the original 2016/17 report, the 2017/18 edition, the 2019/20 global report with its Risk Map spread, and the 2019 Canada edition.

KLDiscovery · 2021 – present · UI/UX Designer

Nebula AI Case Explorer

Making huge document sets legible: product design for an AI-assisted case exploration tool inside Nebula, KLDiscovery's enterprise eDiscovery platform.

View the live product ↗
Role
UI/UX Designer; directed the visual design of AI Case Explorer
Involvement
From the earliest product and engineering discussions through launch and ongoing development
Status
Launched in 2026

The problem

Legal teams in eDiscovery start with an enormous, unstructured pile of documents and very little time to understand it. Case Explorer is an AI tool for early case intelligence: it helps them find the key people, themes, events and timelines before review begins.

My role

  • Directed the visual design of Nebula AI Case Explorer, from the first product and engineering discussions to launch in 2026, taking early concepts and wireframes to finished workflows and visual design.
  • Designed UI and UX across the wider Nebula platform, turning complex legal workflows and very large document sets into clear experiences across the case lifecycle.
  • Leading the visual foundations of a new product design system that grew out of Case Explorer.
  • Mentored two designers through design reviews, critique and ongoing coaching.
  • Introduced AI-assisted workflows (Claude) to speed up prototyping, document the component library and build internal tools such as automated colour-swatch recognition.

Design system

The design system grew out of Case Explorer and gives KLDiscovery a shared foundation of components and patterns. It's planned to roll out to Nebula in 2027, then across three to four more KLDiscovery products.

Outcome

Nebula AI Case Explorer launched in 2026, and its design work became the starting point for a design system planned for Nebula and further KLDiscovery products.
